Opera ottava, Libro primo, A Amsterdam, Spesa di Michele Carlo Le Cene, Libraro' (plate no. 520), the 1725 first edition whose first four concertos are the Four Seasons; this is the viola part-book from the BnF (shelfmark Vm7 1703), with an 18th-century ex-libris inscription and the BnF stamp. Pages 1-10 of the 42-page set are the vellum cover, blank leaves and flyleaves; page 11 is the title page (checked by thumbnail). object.medium: Violin concerto in E major, RV 269, with strings and continuo; engraved first edition
object.description: Antonio Vivaldi, a Venetian priest who taught the violin at the Ospedale della Pietà, an orphanage famous for its girls' orchestra, published twelve concertos in Amsterdam in 1725 under the title 'The Contest of Harmony and Invention'. The first four are the Four Seasons, and each is prefaced by a sonnet, probably by Vivaldi himself, whose lines are printed in the parts at the moments they describe. 'Spring' opens with birdsong traded between three violins, a murmuring brook, a thunderstorm, and then a sleeping goatherd, a barking dog in the violas, and a rustic bagpipe dance. It is among the earliest and most vivid examples of music telling a story, and today the most performed Baroque work of all. The sheet shown is the title page of the 1725 Le Cène edition from the Bibliothèque nationale de France. The visitor hears the first movement, played by John Harrison with the Wichita State University Chamber Players in a live recording from 2000, released under a Creative Commons licence.
facts: The concertos were dedicated to the Bohemian count Wenzel von Morzin, and had probably been circulating in manuscript for several years before publication.
Each season carries a sonnet, with letters in the score linking lines of verse to passages of music, such as 'the barking dog' for the viola in the Largo.
Vivaldi's reputation collapsed after his death in 1741 and the Four Seasons were almost unknown until the 1940s, when the first recordings appeared.
